description: A deputy general counsel must approve the company's response to a sanctions-screening anomaly, including whether to make a voluntary disclosure, the scope of the disclosure, and the operating restrictions for the overseas distributor.

shared_context.S1: The company discovered a sanctions-screening anomaly involving payments connected with an overseas distributor.
shared_context.S2: No regulator has contacted the company about the anomaly.
shared_context.S3: The distributor remains commercially important, and the company is preparing a response for its audit committee.
shared_context.S4: Under the company's pre-filing review policy, the deputy general counsel conducts a cross-functional check with compliance, sanctions, and commercial operations before approving any board or regulator recommendation.

PF1.text: Daniel completed transaction testing of the payment records and confirmed that exactly 3 payments totaling $184,600 passed through the distributor's intermediary during the review period; he has not yet circulated the testing worksheet because the compliance review is still awaiting his sign-off.

PF2.text: Maya's review of the current OFAC guidance concluded that the appropriate filing path for these facts is an expressly labeled voluntary self-disclosure, rather than an ordinary explanatory inquiry; she completed the analysis yesterday but held it for the cross-functional review because the filing decision had not yet been requested.

PF3.text: Tom confirmed in this week's call with the business sponsor that the distributor may continue only if intermediary payments stop and invoices are paid directly to the distributor; the sponsor requires this direct-invoicing arrangement and will not approve terminating the distributor.

acceptance_conditions: The company must make a filing to OFAC.
The filing must be expressly identified as a voluntary self-disclosure.
The filing must report exactly 3 transactions totaling exactly $184,600.
Enhanced sanctions screening must apply for exactly 12 months.
The distributor may continue only with intermediary payments stopped and direct invoicing.
The plan must include a direct-invoicing commitment.
The compliance transaction testing must be cited as justification for the reported transaction count and amount.

decisive_facts.why: The shared anomaly has no stated scope or value; PF1 changes the filing from an unspecified report to exactly 3 transactions totaling exactly $184,600 and supplies the required cited testing basis.
The absence of regulator contact does not identify a filing path; PF2 changes the response to an OFAC filing expressly labeled as a voluntary self-disclosure.

The distributor's commercial importance alone does not determine its operating terms; PF3 changes the plan to continued distribution with intermediary payments stopped, direct invoicing, and a matching commitment.
